From: Marta Russo <marta@datascale.com>

Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@datascale.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@datascale.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA alignment: monthly remedy cap request

Ben —

Thanks for walking through the draft SOW yesterday. DataScale is excited about moving forward, but procurement and legal asked us to surface one remaining concern on the SLA: the combination of uptime commitment at 99.99% plus Redwood's unrestricted monthly crediting mechanism creates a payback exposure that our finance team isn't comfortable with for the early months of the contract.

Concretely, they're asking whether Redwood can consider:
- lowering the baseline uptime commitment to 99.95% for the first 3 months of production (pilot), or
- alternatively, keeping 99.99% but capping the aggregate monthly service credit at 20% of the monthly invoice for months 1–3.

We also need clarity on how maintenance windows, regional failovers, and short transient spikes are measured/credited — our SRE worried about cumulative-minute buckets during repeated short incidents.

Can you propose a pragmatic path that limits DataScale's short-term downside while keeping a firm production SL for the long run? If helpful, attaching the procurement team's redlines (SLA_Redwood_Template_v3.docx).

Appreciate a quick reply — vendor selection timeline is next week.

—Marta
Procurement Manager
DataScale Systems

Subject: Re: SLA alignment: monthly remedy cap request

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. Short answer: yes, we can offer a compromise that protects DataScale's short-term exposure while preserving service incentives. Two options we typically propose for pilots:

Option A (pilot grace-band):
- Maintain 99.99% for production, but for months 1–3 treat a reduced enforcement band: only cumulative downtime over 2 hours/month ("grace-band") triggers credits.
- If triggered, credits calculated per the standard ladder but capped at 20% of the monthly invoice for months 1–3.

Option B (temporary baseline):
- Reduce baseline to 99.95% for months 1–3; standard credit ladder applies above that baseline with a monthly cap of 30%.

Operational notes we can add to either approach:
- Maintenance windows scheduled with 72 hours notice and not counted toward downtime.
- Transient spikes under 2 minutes are ignored; repeated short incidents are aggregated into a rolling 24-hour bucket to avoid gaming.

I looped in Marissa and Laura to confirm commercial/contracting feasibility. If preferred, we can put Option A into the SOW and include a three-month review to revert or tighten the band.

Happy to hop on a short call today.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts

Folks — forwarding the ask from DataScale. Procurement wants either a temporary baseline (99.95% for three months) or a cap on monthly credits. My recommended stance: go with Option A (grace-band + 20% cap for months 1–3). Rationale:

- Preserves our 99.99% commitment publicly while limiting immediate commercial exposure.
- Keeps incentives aligned: credits still trigger for sustained incidents ( >2 hours cumulative ).
- Gives us a clear review window after Q1 of production to reassess once traffic stabilizes.

Key negotiation levers for legal: define the exact aggregation rule for repeated short incidents (suggest rolling 24-hour aggregation with a 2-minute floor per event) and make maintenance carveouts explicit.

Marissa: is a 20% cap for months 1–3 commercially acceptable?
Laura: can you confirm contracting language we should put in the SOW to safely implement the rolling aggregation and maintenance carveouts? I want to avoid opening a broad "event aggregation" ambiguous clause.

Ben
Account Exec

Ben/Marissa —

Agree with Option A as the primary path. Draft language below that legal is comfortable with and minimizes ambiguity:

1) Pilot grace-band and cap
- For months 1–3 following GA, Redwood will maintain a 99.99% availability target. However, customer acknowledges a "pilot grace-band" such that credits will only be calculated when cumulative customer-impacting downtime exceeds 120 minutes in any billing month.
- If credits are triggered during the pilot months, aggregate monthly credits will be capped at 20% of the monthly invoice.

2) Event aggregation and measurement
- Individual incidents shorter than two minutes will not independently trigger a credit.
- Repeated incidents will be aggregated into a rolling 24-hour window for the purpose of calculating cumulative downtime.
- Scheduled maintenance (published at least 72 hours in advance) and force majeure are carveouts.

3) Review clause
- Parties will conduct a joint review after the pilot period (within 30 days of the end of month 3) to reassess the grace-band and cap. Any permanent change to the baseline uptime or cap requires written amendment to the SOW.

If you want, I can create a tracked-change SOW snippet (SLA_Redwood_Template_v3.docx) that embeds this language. Once Ben gets put-on-record from DataScale that 20% cap + 120-minute grace is an acceptable compromise, we can finalize.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
